steps.prompt: What do the first two have in common that the last two do not?
options: they warn the listener that something difficult is coming, before saying what
they ask for a specific change
steps.answer: they warn the listener that something difficult is coming, before saying what

steps.prompt: Make the request softer. Choose the version you would actually use.
options: Would you mind to look at it again?
Would you mind having another look at it?
steps.answer: Would you mind having another look at it?

steps.prompt: Make the request softer. Choose the version you would actually use.
options: Could you tell me who should I speak to?
Could you tell me who I should speak to?
steps.answer: Could you tell me who I should speak to?

steps.prompt: Make the request softer. Choose the version you would actually use.
options: I was wondering can you replace it.
I was wondering whether you could replace it.
steps.answer: I was wondering whether you could replace it.

steps.prompt: Make the request softer. Choose the version you would actually use.
options: Is there any chance of a refund?
Is there any chance to refund?
steps.answer: Is there any chance of a refund?

steps.title: Which version would you actually use? Choose the better one.
steps.prompt: A colleague keeps leaving dirty cups out.
options: You always leave your cups out. It’s disgusting.
It would really help if you could wash your mugs before you go.
Somebody in this office is very untidy.
steps.answer: It would really help if you could wash your mugs before you go.

steps.title: Which version would you actually use? Choose the better one.
steps.prompt: You need to open a difficult conversation.
options: I’m sorry to have to say this, but there’s something I’m not happy about.
steps.answer: I’m sorry to have to say this, but there’s something I’m not happy about.

steps.title: Which version would you actually use? Choose the better one.
steps.prompt: A colleague takes personal calls at their desk all day.
options: Would you mind taking those calls in your own time?
You never think about anybody else.
steps.answer: Would you mind taking those calls in your own time?

steps.title: Which version would you actually use? Choose the better one.
steps.prompt: Something you bought a few weeks ago has stopped working.
options: Sorry to bother you, but I’ve got a bit of a problem with this tablet.
I want to see the manager.
steps.answer: Sorry to bother you, but I’ve got a bit of a problem with this tablet.

steps.title: Check your own post. Which of them did you do?
steps.model: Opening: I’m sorry to have to say this, but… · Look, it’s a bit awkward, but… · Sorry to bother you, but…

steps.title: Отметь, чему научился
items: ✓ use the words of a group in disagreement — irritated, campaign, database, devote, closed off
✓ use the phrasal verbs — come up with, look up, make out, put up, look forward to
✓ warn somebody that a difficult thing is coming
✓ ask for a specific change — It would really help if… / Would you mind…ing?
✓ complain about the behaviour rather than the person, and avoid always and never
✓ agree before you disagree — I see your point, but… / That’s a fair point
